content: 1. Initiating IMOD therapy is generally contraindicated in patients concurrently receiving QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 2. Both paliperidone and posaconazole increase the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 3. Posaconazole elevates panobinostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Reduce the starting dose of panobinostat to 10 mg when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 4. Pantoprazole reduces the efficacy of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Use caution and monitor. 5. Posaconazole increases paricalcitol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 6. Both paroxetine and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 7. Posaconazole and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 8. Posaconazole increases perampanel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 9. Both perphenazine and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 10. Phenobarbital reduces posaconazole levels by increasing its metabolism and through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. 11. Phenytoin decreases posaconazole levels by enhancing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 12. Posaconazole increases polatuzumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related metabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase unconjugated MMAE exposure, raising the risk of toxicities. 13. Ponatinib increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. 14. Posaconazole increases praziquantel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 15. Posaconazole increases prednisolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 16. Posaconazole increases prednisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 17. Both primaquine and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 18. Primidone reduces posaconazole levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Both prochlorperazine and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 20. Posaconazole increases progesterone intravaginal gel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 21. Posaconazole increases micronized progesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 22. Posaconazole increases natural progesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 23. Both promazine and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 24. Both promethazine and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 25. Both protriptyline and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 26. Posaconazole increases quazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 27. Quercetin reduces posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. 28. Posaconazole increases quetiapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs can increase each other’s toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. Avoid use in patients with QT-prolonging drugs or risk factors for prolonged QT intervals. Postmarketing cases have reported QT prolongation with overdose in patients with concomitant illness or drugs causing electrolyte imbalance or QT prolongation. 29. Both posaconazole and quinine prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 30. Posaconazole increases quizartinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Adjust quizartinib dosage to 4 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Interrupt quizartinib during strong CYP3A inhibitor use. Both drugs can increase each other’s effects via QTc interval prolongation. Monitor patients more frequently with ECG if co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 31. Rabeprazole reduces posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Use caution and monitor. 32. Ranolazine increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 33. Posaconazole increases repaglinide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 34. Rifabutin reduces posaconazole levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 35. Rifampin reduces posaconazole levels by increasing its metabolism and through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. 36. Posaconazole increases rifaximin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. 37. Posaconazole increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. No rilpivirine dose adjustment is required. Rilpivirine increases posaconazole toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 38. Posaconazole increases ripretinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), raising the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor. 39. Both posaconazole and risperidone prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 40. Posaconazole increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. 41. Posaconazole increases roflumilast topical levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 42. Posaconazole increases romidepsin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 43. Posaconazole increases salmeterol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Sarecycline increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates, which may require dosage reduction when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 45. Posaconazole increases saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Adjust saxagliptin dosage to 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 46. Posaconazole increases seladelpar levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Exercise caution in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers and are co-administered a moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 47. Selpercatinib increases posaconazole toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor. 48. Both sertraline and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 49. Posaconazole increases sildenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 50. Simvastatin increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. 51. Sirolimus increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. 52. Sodium bicarbonate reduces posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Use caution and monitor. 53. Sodium citrate/citric acid reduces posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Use caution and monitor. 54. Both posaconazole and sodium sulfate/potassium chloride/magnesium sulfate/polyethylene glycol reduce serum potassium levels. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 55. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate reduces posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Administer drugs at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. 56. Posaconazole increases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 57. Posaconazole increases solifenacin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 58. Both sorafenib and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 59. St. John’s Wort reduces posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. 60. Stiripentol increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Consider reducing the dose of P-glycoprotein substrates if adverse reactions occur when co-administered with stiripentol. 61. Posaconazole increases sufentanil SL levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentration, potentially leading to prolonged or severe adverse effects, including fatal respiratory depression. Use caution and monitor. 62. Both sulfamethoxazole and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 63. Posaconazole increases sunitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 64. Posaconazole increases tacrolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Tacrolimus increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. 65. Posaconazole increases tadalafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 66. Posaconazole increases talazoparib levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Talazoparib is a P-glycoprotein substrate, and co-administration with P-gp inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. Use caution and monitor. 67. Posaconazole increases tamoxifen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inhibition reduces tamoxifen metabolism to N-desmethyl tamoxifen, an active metabolite with similar biological activity. Use caution and monitor. 68. Posaconazole increases tasimelteon levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 69. Both posaconazole and telavancin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 70. Posaconazole increases temsirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 71. Posaconazole increases terbinafine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 72. Posaconazole increases tezacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Adjust tezacaftor dosage regimen if co-administered with a strong CYP3A inhibitor. 73. Posaconazole increases theophylline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 74. Both thioridazine and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 75. Posaconazole increases ticagrelor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ticagrelor is metabolized by CYP3A4/5. Avoid use with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 76. Posaconazole increases tinidazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 77. Posaconazole increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 78. Posaconazole increases tisotumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Its active metabolite (MMAE) is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase unconjugated MMAE systemic exposure, raising the risk of adverse effects. Use caution and monitor. 79. Posaconazole increases tolterodine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 80. Tolvaptan increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. 81. Posaconazole increases toremifene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Toremifene metabolism may be inhibited by drugs that inhibit CYP3A4 hepatic enzymes. Use caution and monitor. 82. Trazodone reduces posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 83. Posaconazole increases triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 84. Posaconazole increases triazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 85. Both trifluoperazine and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 86. Both posaconazole and trimethoprim prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 87. Both trimipramine and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Posaconazole also increases trimipramine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 88. Both posaconazole and tropisetron prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 89. Tucatinib increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor.
